delivery.description: The delivery ULID. Matches X-Tmesis-Delivery. Duplicated in the body so a receiver that logs bodies has the dedupe key without the headers.

occurred_at.description: RFC3339 UTC, when the event happened on the node. ORDER BY THIS, never by arrival: delivery is unordered.

session.description: The session this recording belongs to (one file, one session, as built). Correlate on recording_id.

stage.description: CLOSED set: which step failed. It drives routing, because a capture failure and an upload failure are different investigations. As built for the ingest artifact: capture is a file that never opened (disk floor, create failure, a part the ledger assigned to another writer), finalize is a row a dead process left whose file is gone at boot or a close whose ledger write was refused (the file is complete on disk and kept; nothing uploads or registers it), upload is a destination that failed permanently or past the retry budget with the file kept, register is a finalized file that cannot be read back.

reason.description: One sentence. Free text, because the useful part is the underlying ffmpeg or S3 message.

raw_parts_preserved.description: true means the captured source parts are still on the node and a human can recover from them. false means there was nothing to preserve.

parts.description: How many parts the artifact had when it failed. Always 1 as built: one row is one file (final plan 11.34 D4).

path.description: Where the preserved raw parts are, when raw_parts_preserved is true. null otherwise. The schema enforces the recovery invariant: a non-null path requires raw_parts_preserved true, and a null path requires raw_parts_preserved false (crossfield tag, pinned by TestRecordingFailedSchemaAcceptsTheDocumentedPayload).
